outcome: Correlation with rates of caesarean section (CS)
Correlation with rates of trial of labour after CS (TOLAC)
cohort: Women with complete uterine rupture identified from the International Network of Obstetric Survey Systems (INOSS) database, totaling 864 women out of 2,625,017 deliveries
finding: Higher prevalence of complete uterine ruptures per TOLAC was observed in countries with low previous CS and high TOLAC rates, while rates of hysterectomy and perinatal death are about 10% following complete uterine rupture, but extremely low (2.2 and 3.2 per 10,000 TOLACs, respectively) for women undergoing TOLAC.
mod_finding: The prevalence of complete uterine ruptures was higher in countries with low previous cesarean section rates and high rates of trial of labor after cesarean section.
